article_title: Development and validation of a cost-effective DIY simulation model for McDonald cerclage training.
citation: Buechel J, Kalisz A, Herbert S-L, Scherer-Quenzer A, Blau-Schneider B, Starrach T, Kraft K, Wöckel A, Pecks U, Kiesel M. (2024). Development and validation of a cost-effective DIY simulation model for McDonald cerclage training. Archives of Gynecology and Obstetrics. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00404-024-07812-8
title: Wuerzburg Cervical Cerclage Simulator (WCCS)
description: The WCCS is a DIY McDonald cerclage trainer built from a 10 cm drainpipe simulating the vagina, foamed plastic vaginal walls, and two 3D-printed, silicone-duplicated cervix models: a closed cervix for prophylactic cerclage and a cervix "already opened to 1.5 cm with bulging membranes" simulated with a water-filled balloon. It weighs 1110 g, mounts on a desk or examination couch, and cost 39.64 EUR to produce.
requirements: Standard surgical instruments and a light source such as a headlamp or examination light are needed to perform the procedure on the model.
Cervix models must be replaced after multiple uses; each silicone cervix is usable for approximately five to 10 cerclage procedures.
constraints: The WCCS is only suitable for the McDonald technique, not the Shirodkar technique.
The materials do not accurately replicate the haptic properties of cervical and vaginal tissue.
The model was optimized for braided Mersilene sutures and was tested only with them.
target_learners: obstetricians and gynecologists training in McDonald cerclage
target_learning_goals: performing McDonald cerclage stitches for prophylactic and emergency indications
examples: Thirteen obstetricians from four German university hospitals performed McDonald cerclage on the simulator with standard instruments and rated it on a 7-point Likert scale.
